note: A RATCHET, not a target. The gate fails when errors RISE above this, never when they merely stay put. A hard zero would block every commit today; a ratchet stops the regression that actually happened -- a format-string rule that was never called survived two commits because nothing compiled the 23 modules it broke.
lower_me: When errors fall, lower this. That is the whole mechanism.
why_the_totals_moved: Lowered from 27 on 2026-08-02 after the unhandled-guard fix, which compared the LENGTH of a counter and so caught only the first site of any construct. Two errors went with it, including a `for` loop with no iterable. Lowering when errors fall IS the mechanism; leaving it high would have banked the win as slack.
